14.0.s.en: (1) The visit of Jeroboam's wife to Ahijah

14.0.0.en: After God warned Jeroboam to turn back from the worship of idols and he did not repent, He sent him a severe affliction, hoping it would awaken him: the illness of his son Abijah, who was perhaps his firstborn. This was contrary to his human arrangements, for he had been a successful administrative leader who had planned everything carefully in order to leave his kingdom to his son as an inheritance. Yet now the son falls ill and then dies, so that God might teach him that he must rely on Him and not on his own strength, and that he might turn from the worship of idols to God.

14.1.0.en: Shiloh: It lies south of Shechem and north of Jerusalem, and the tabernacle of God was there, so the prophet Ahijah and other believers who held fast to the worship of God and rejected idols dwelt in it. Jeroboam asked his wife to go to Shiloh to meet the prophet Ahijah, who had previously told him that he would reign over the people of Israel (ch. 11:29), and he asked her to disguise herself so that no one would know that he was resorting to the prophet.

14.1.1.en: We notice several matters in his asking his wife to disguise herself:

14.1.2.en: 1- His awareness of his sins, which anger God, and of God's judgment upon them; yet he did not want to repent. He wanted only his own interests, namely reassurance about his son's recovery, and he feared that Ahijah would refuse to answer him.

14.1.3.en: 2- Because he was deceitful and wicked, he did not trust any of his servants, so he sent his wife, since the son's recovery mattered to her as it did to him.

14.1.4.en: 3- He believed that Ahijah was a prophet able to know the future by the power of God, yet in ignorance he thought he could deceive him by his wife's disguise.

14.1.5.en: 4- He did not want his people to know that he was taking refuge with a prophet of God, because he did not want them to return to the temple of God and His prophets, lest they leave him and his idols.

14.1.6.en: 5- In Jeroboam's heart there was faith that God alone is the true God, so he sent to learn His voice concerning the recovery of his son, and he did not ask his idols, because he did not believe in them, even though he had deceived his people and told them, "This is the image of God."

14.2.0.en: He asked her to take some simple gifts that were usually presented when meeting the prophets, as an expression of the honor due to them, for he is able to ask God, who would reveal to him the fate of his son.

14.3.0.en: His eyes were set: His eyes grew very weak, or he lost his sight completely.

14.3.1.en: Jeroboam's wife did what her husband had asked of her and went to the house of Ahijah in Shiloh, and Ahijah's sight had grown dim through old age.

14.4.0.en: The Lord informed him of the identity of the woman coming to him, of the reason for her coming, and that she would be disguised so that the prophet would not know who she was, and then He told him what to say. Thus we see that the power of God perfects His children however great their weakness, and even reveals to them what the strong cannot know. His inability to see did not prevent him from knowing the truth about the queen, the wife of Jeroboam, who was in disguise.

14.4.1.en: As long as you are with God, do not be troubled by any weakness that befalls you, for God is able to compensate you for it, so that you become stronger than the strong. He arranges your affairs, gives you all your needs, and reveals to you the greatest thing, which is His love and the knowledge of Him.

14.5.0.en: As soon as the Lord finished speaking to Ahijah, he sensed the woman's coming and heard the sound of her feet at the door, so he received her by name, saying to her, "O wife of Jeroboam." He told her that there was no need for disguise and that he had for her tidings that were not at all pleasant. Thus everyone who lies to God or deceives Him must expect an angry reaction from God, because he treats Him lightly.

14.6.0.en: Ahijah told Jeroboam's wife a message from God to her husband, in which He reminds him that it was He who raised him from being a fugitive in Egypt, despised, to the throne of Israel, and who tore the kingdom of David apart and gave him the greater part of it. God attributes the kingdom to David even though he had died and his grandson Jeroboam was reigning over it, because of David's piety, his keeping of God's commandments and his uprightness; therefore God blessed him and blessed the kingdom for his sake. But when Jeroboam sinned, he gave him a part of it and gave a part to Rehoboam. Yet Jeroboam learned nothing from the virtues of David and his piety; he did not worship God with all his heart, but walked in evil and worshiped idols.

14.6.1.en: Here we find that God calls Himself "the Lord God of Israel," for He still loves His people despite their departure from Him. He calls Himself their God in order to call them to repentance, but if they persist in their sins He will forsake them and leave the nations to discipline them.

14.6.2.en: God also reminded him that he had committed terrible sins, more than all who were before him. Solomon sinned by having many wives and honoring his wives by setting up idols for their gods, but he continued to worship God in His temple. Jeroboam, however, cut off his relation to worship in the temple of God and made idols, namely the golden calves, and claimed that they were his gods and the gods of the people, and he bowed down to them and even served as a priest to them.

14.7.0.en: Him that pisseth against the wall: every male.

14.7.1.en: Him that is shut up and left: the slaves and the free, or the imprisoned and the free; the meaning is everyone.

14.7.3.en: Then God pronounced His punishment on Jeroboam: that all his offspring and all the males, that is, those who could reign after him, would be destroyed, and He would be rid of them as a man is rid of the waste of animals. They would be killed and their corpses cast out, and no one would bury them because of the intensity of fear, for Baasha, the king who would come to the throne of Israel, would destroy all the offspring of Jeroboam (ch. 15:29). Just as Jeroboam rejected the worship of God and led his people astray, so God rejects him and destroys all his offspring.

14.8.0.en: The prophet asked Jeroboam's wife to return to her house, and he foretold to her that as soon as she entered the city her son would die.

14.9.0.en: The Lord found in Abijah the son of Jeroboam something good. Perhaps he rejected his father's idols and still prayed with his face toward Jerusalem, where the temple of God was. For this reason the Lord had mercy on him by his death, that he might be buried with honor and not be overtaken by the shame that would overtake his father and the rest of his family, as the Scripture says, "The righteous is taken away from the evil to come" (Isa 57:1).

14.10.0.en: That day: that is, very soon.

14.10.1.en: But what? even now: that is, God will not say more and is content with what He has said, because the execution will be swift. The Lord chooses for Himself another king whom He sets over Israel and who will cut off the house of Jeroboam, namely King Baasha. The Lord decreed that the time for the fulfillment of this prophecy would come very soon; for after the death of Jeroboam his son Nadab reigned for two years, and then Baasha rose against him and killed him and all the offspring of Jeroboam, and reigned in his place.

14.11.0.en: As a reed is shaken in the water: the reed is the cane, or the rush that is planted along watercourses, and because of its lightness it shakes violently when the winds blow upon it.

14.11.1.en: Beyond the river: that is, to Nineveh, which is on the river Euphrates, and all the cities of Assyria that belong to it.

14.11.2.en: Their groves: the plural of the grove, a tall piece of wood set up on high places for the worship of idols.

14.11.3.en: The divine punishment extends to the whole kingdom of Israel and not only to the offspring of Jeroboam, because all the kings of Israel walked in the worship of the idols that Jeroboam made. So the kingdom of Assyria attacked them and took them captive in three stages, 230 years after the reign of Jeroboam (2 Kgs 17), and at that time all the people of Israel will be in great distress, shaking like the shaking of a reed in the water. God takes the land of Canaan that He gave to His people and gives it to Assyria, while His people in the kingdom of Israel are scattered in the land of Assyria, especially since they went on and on in worshiping foreign gods, for the golden calves of Jeroboam encouraged them to worship many other gods.

14.12.s.en: (2) The death of Jeroboam and his son

14.12.0.en: Tirzah: a city of beautiful appearance, lying northeast of Shechem at a distance of 11.5 km.

14.12.1.en: Jeroboam's wife returned to the king's residence in the city of Tirzah, to which he had moved from Shechem, the capital. Perhaps it was a resting place for the king because of its beauty and not a second capital. The king remained in Shechem and Tirzah until King Omri built the city of Samaria and moved the capital to it (ch. 16:23, 24). When the feet of Jeroboam's wife touched the threshold of the door, which may have been the gate of the city or the door of her house, her son died, and they buried him and made lamentation for him, as the prophet Ahijah had told her. The prophecy was fulfilled, and this was an incentive from God to Jeroboam and his house to repent of their sins, because the death of the boy announces that the rest of the prophecy would also be fulfilled. But sadly Jeroboam did not repent; he continued in the worship of idols and also made war against the kingdom of Judah (v. 19).

14.13.0.en: Jeroboam walked in evil and entered into wars with Rehoboam and his son Abijah, the kings of Judah (v. 30, 2 Chr 13:3-20). In them Jeroboam was defeated and Abijah took from him many cities such as Bethel. Jeroboam reigned for 22 years, and then the Lord struck him with an illness and he died, and this shows God's anger against him. Then his son Nadab reigned for two years, and after him the family of Jeroboam came to an end, for all his offspring were killed, that the word of God which He spoke by the mouth of Ahijah might be fulfilled.

14.13.1.en: The book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel is not the book of Chronicles found in the Holy Bible, but a book in which the records of the kings of Israel were written.

14.13.2.en: Do not persist in evil and anger God, but learn from the events of life that pass over you, so that you may take heed and repent, for God desires your salvation. So return to Him, because He loves you.

14.14.s.en: (3) The evils of Rehoboam, his wars and his death

14.14.0.en: While Jeroboam was reigning over ten tribes in Israel, Rehoboam the son of Solomon was reigning in Judah over two tribes (the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin). Rehoboam was 41 years old when he took the throne, and he reigned 17 years; the capital of his kingdom was Jerusalem, and his mother was "Naamah," who was of the children of Ammon. If Solomon reigned for 40 years, this means that he begot Rehoboam before he became king, so he was probably the firstborn, and the influence of his Gentile mother is evident, for he worshiped idols and built temples for them, as appears in the following verses, even though he was in Jerusalem, the city that God chose so that His temple and worship would be in it alone. God's choosing Jerusalem so that His name would be called upon it shows the enormity of the sin of Rehoboam, and before him of his father Solomon, in placing statues of foreign gods in it for the people to worship.

14.15.0.en: They provoked him to jealousy: they stirred up His jealousy, that is, they angered Him.

14.15.1.en: At that time the people of Judah were doing evil, and they angered the Lord more than all that their fathers had done, by their many sins. God likens His people to a bride and Himself to her bridegroom, so when she sins by worshiping other pagan gods she defies Him, angers Him and stirs up His jealousy as her bridegroom, and He becomes angry with her. This is what the kingdom of Judah did by worshiping idols in the days of Rehoboam, as will appear in the next two verses.

14.16.0.en: High places: altars on the tops of hills whose use God forbade (Deut 12:11, 13). Images: sacred pillars for the idols in the form of statues.

14.16.1.en: The people of God built for themselves, on the hills and under the trees, images and pillars for their pagan worship; that is, the pagan worship of the gods of heaven spread on the hills and under every tree that had great shade, so the pagan gods were many, and all this in the holy city of God, Jerusalem, and its surroundings. This shows how far the people had departed from the worship of God.

14.17.0.en: Sodomites: the passive partner in sexual perversion between two men.

14.17.1.en: In their worship of idols, and to please the gods, they practiced sexual perversion between men, and of course they also practiced fornication before that, so there were women and men consecrated to fornication in the temples of the pagan gods, and their earnings were given to the temples of the gods. This shows the depth of degradation to which the people of God had come, for they had become like the nations whom God drove out of the land of Canaan before His people dwelt in it.

14.17.2.en: Beware of leaving God and His Church and immersing yourself in the world and its lusts, for the teachings of the Church condemn you if you neglect them. Why do you sink into evil like the people of the world?! Be strong and walk uprightly, and you will be the light of the world and the salt of the earth, confident that God will support you and protect you.

14.18.s.en: (4) Rehoboam and his wars against Shishak and against Jeroboam

14.18.0.en: Came up: because the land of Judah is higher than the land of Egypt.

14.18.1.en: In the fifth year of the reign of Rehoboam, Shishak came, the founder of the Twenty-second Dynasty in Egypt, and he was the most dangerous enemy to invade the land of Israel since the days of King Saul. Jeroboam had summoned him to support him and establish his power against Rehoboam king of Judah, so he attacked the kingdom of Judah and seized a number of its towns, and he also subdued some cities belonging to the northern kingdom, which were under the authority of the Canaanites, and gave them to his ally Jeroboam, who had lived in Egypt for a period of time under Shishak's protection. All this Shishak recorded on the walls of the temples of Karnak. This shows the departure of both the northern and southern kingdoms of the children of Israel from God and their reliance on the powers of the world, which caused God to forsake them, so they fell into trials. In Rehoboam's reign the kingdom was divided, and Jeroboam died of illness and his offspring were cut off, as we mentioned before, and here Shishak disciplines the people of God.

14.19.0.en: It was the custom of the people at that time to keep their jewels by depositing them in trust in the temple; so Shishak seized the treasures of the temple and the treasures of the royal palace, and he also took the shields of gold that Solomon had made.

14.19.1.en: If you are lax with sin, Satan will rob you of all the virtues and abilities you possess and humiliate you. So hold fast to your relationship with God, so that Satan may fear you, God may keep you, and you may live in peace.

14.20.1.en: Since gold was not as plentiful in this period as it was in the days of Solomon, Rehoboam substituted shields of bronze for them and committed them to the hand of the guard of the royal palace. So whenever the king entered the temple, the soldiers would bring the shields there, and when the king departed they would return them to their storehouse.

14.21.0.en: The rest of the acts of Rehoboam and all that he did are written in "the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah." The book of chronicles meant is not the one found in the Holy Bible, but books in which the records of the kings were written, as some details about the life of Rehoboam were mentioned in the Second Book of Chronicles (2 Chr 10:12).

14.22.0.en: There was never any agreement between the two parts of the divided kingdom, Judah and Israel, throughout the reign of the two kings, Rehoboam in Judah and Jeroboam in Israel, for they remained continually in wars and disputes.

14.23.0.en: Rehoboam died and was buried with his fathers in the city of David. His mother was "Naamah the Ammonitess." His son Abijam, who is also called "Abijah," succeeded him on the throne.

14.23.1.en: The First Book of Kings. Abijah and Asa reign over Judah, and Nadab and Baasha over Israel
